summary: The narrator, a fugitive wanted for mass murder, is confronted by two mall security guards after being caught with an alcoholic drink she appears to be underage to have. Her resemblance to a notorious killer, the 'psycho from the paper,' spreads through the crowd, the guards back away, and sirens approach. She escapes by climbing potted-plant shelves onto the roof and running off the building. The passage is an excerpt from Book 2, part 96.
one_line: A fugitive mistaken for a mass murderer escapes mall security and sirens by leaping onto a rooftop.
key_facts: The narrator had self-medicated enough to stabilize her world for the moment.
The narrator had left an ID in her stash in the drywall of the Chinatown apartment and thought she probably still had it.
Two security guards confronted the narrator over a half-drunk bottle on the ground and suspected underage drinking.
The narrator said, "I swear I'm over twenty-one," and offered to leave.
The female security guard radioed for help with a walkie and told the narrator to stay where she was.
The narrator was carrying an illegal Ruger tucked in the back of her belt and grenades in her pockets.
A dark-skinned, curly-haired woman shrieked, "The psycho from the paper! You caught her!"
The male guard said, "She does look like it," after comparing the narrator's features to the suspect.
The guards began backing away, deciding their rent-a-cop duties were not worth risking their lives against a homicidal maniac.
Sirens began sounding from not too far away.
A crowd of onlookers gathered around the narrator at a healthy radius, and at least two people pulled out mobile phones.
The narrator ran up a display of potted plants against the wall as if they were stairs.
The narrator cleared the eaves in a dive, rolled onto the flat rooftop, and ran off the back of the building.
